uncited: The Phase Function Interface defines the abstract contract for phase functions in the pbrt rendering system, requiring implementations to evaluate the scattering probability density and sample new scattering directions.
The interface operates on unit direction vectors $\omega_o$ (outgoing) and $\omega_i$ (incident) and random variables $u$.
It outputs a scalar probability density value or a sampled direction.
The core data structure is the abstract base class `PhaseFunction`.

2.  `Sample_p(const Vector3f &wo, Vector3f *wi, const Point2f &u)`: Samples a new incident direction $\omega_i$ given an outgoing direction $\omega_o$ and 2D uniform random numbers $u$, returning the probability density of the sampled direction.
pbrt uses the convention that both $\omega_o$ and $\omega_i$ point **away** from the scattering point $x$.
Implementers must account for this sign flip when adapting formulas from standard texts.
*   **Direction Convention:** As noted, the sign of the incident direction differs from standard literature.
It is characterized by distinct peaks at 22 and 46 degrees, which create halos when the sun penetrates optically thin cirrus clouds.
The interface itself has $O(1)$ time and memory complexity for evaluation and sampling, as it delegates to specific implementations.
The complexity depends entirely on the subclass (e.g., Henyey-Greenstein is $O(1)$, while tabulated or complex ice models may involve interpolation or lookup).
The direction convention aligns with pbrt's BSDF framework, simplifying integration.
*   **Limitations:** The abstract nature requires careful implementation of sampling algorithms, which can be non-trivial for complex phase functions.
The direction convention may confuse users familiar with standard scattering literature.
Use this interface when implementing custom phase functions within the pbrt framework.
It is suitable for any participating media simulation requiring angular scattering distribution.
The Phase Function Interface was introduced in the pbrt rendering system as part of its volume scattering module.
The interface design reflects pbrt's consistent use of outgoing-direction conventions for all transport quantities.
